title: Threatening Letter
text: “If you’re really a hero, wouldn’t it be simpler to just tell the lord honestly?”

Older Sister was clearly trying to pry as much information out of me as possible. Normally, I supposed it would be wiser not to say anything… but my experience dealing with my Big Sister’s sister told me the opposite was true here—I should speak plainly.
“And if I told her, would she believe me, I wonder? Even now, in this very moment, she doesn’t believe me, does she?”
“Ara, even so, is threatening Big Sister really the way to go about it?”

“For now, I simply called out to you, indeed. If you won’t believe me, my next step is to go explain myself to the lord directly. Of course, if that fails, I’ll just make sure no one can move as far as the shore. To continue, I don’t want the nobles of Melromarc getting the idea that my rampaging gives them some righteous cause, so this is very much a last resort.”
“I see—so if you really are a hero, it looks like you’re trying to deal with the people here by force.”
Older Sister didn’t believe me, but she was playing along regardless. I could feel that attitude radiating off her unmistakably.
Ahh… Father. If it were you, Father, I wished you could tell me how to negotiate in a way that would actually get someone to believe me.
‘No one’s going to easily believe some guy claiming he came from the future. It’s an unreasonable request to begin with.’
That was the sort of thing the Father from my first world—the one I’d failed to save, the one I’d hurt—would probably say, and the words floated up in my mind.
‘Well… it is tough, isn’t it. But it’s not like you can just give up either… I suppose persuasion was impossible from the start.’

The kind Father would likely answer in much the same troubled way. And yet, I felt like that kind Father was praising me, somehow, for refusing to give up. Still, it felt as though both Fathers, from both memories, were teaching me the same lesson in unison: that trying to persuade Older Sister was not a mistake. Even if it ended in failure, it wouldn’t be meaningless.
“Earlier you said Big Sister should just pretend to have a hangover, but even if Big Sister can’t move on her own, they’ll just carry her onto the boat anyway, won’t they?”
Ngh… She was right. Given how tightly-knit the fishermen were, they’d simply arrange some other means of transporting her until the hangover passed.
“I need you to somehow make that not happen, indeed.”
“It’s troubling when Big Sister gets asked to do the impossible—frankly, that’s just absurd.”
“I’m well aware of that, indeed!”
‘Waa… there he goes, getting defensive.’
I felt like the kind Father was saying that somewhere in my head, but honestly, this was about the extent of my thinking. Still, Older Sister’s eyes seemed a little less wary than before.
“You really are remarkably honest—even Big Sister’s surprised.”
“A clumsy lie wouldn’t work on you, so I’m being honest, indeed.”
“Too honest, if you ask me. It puts Big Sister in quite the bind. Whether I resist or report you, Big Sister ends up in trouble either way. Whatever should I do…”
Hmm, Older Sister groaned, mulling it over.
“Too strong a bond breeds tragedy, indeed.”

Originally, it was precisely because Éclair’s parents and the villagers were bound so tightly together that I found myself in this predicament. If going forward as planned meant everyone would die, then don’t unite so stubbornly, indeed!
“I need you to understand how much consideration and effort I’m putting into this, indeed.”
“Really, Big Sister is at a loss here.”
Older Sister broke into a cold sweat.

“To be frank with you, Big Sister, your strength—even accounting for what happens in the future—is simply not what one would call ordinary for a fisherman. And you claim your past is nothing much, yet I can’t help but feel you’re hiding something, indeed.”
“…Ara.”

For some reason, Older Sister gave a small laugh at my words, looking almost pleased that I knew nothing about her past. No, that wasn’t quite right. There was something in her gaze that seemed tinged with a bit of mockery, too. Really, just who was this woman? Was she lying to me? It reminded me of how Elephant and Panda used to take pride in having no notable past to speak of.
“If we’re talking threats, then how about this: if you won’t listen, I’ll take the person who raised you like a parent hostage. Would that make you listen, I wonder?”

Whoa, Older Sister’s glare turned absolutely murderous. So it seemed she truly did cherish Big Sister’s family. No doubt Older Sister had been some orphan wandering the streets once, and Big Sister’s parents had raised her dearly, like a daughter of their own.
“A foster parent and a benefactor, I’d wager. Precisely because I know how much you cherish them, this threat carries weight, indeed.”
“Haah… You really just want the departure delayed by two more days, is that right?”
Older Sister confirmed, her tone laced with a touch of anger.
“Of course, indeed. Do you have some method in mind?”

“There’s no gentle way to go about it. Even if Big Sister threw a tantrum about not wanting to go out, the other fishermen in the village would set sail regardless… though of course, Big Sister is the best among them.”
I was boxed in on all sides. Curse you, Éclair’s parents! I wanted them to know just how much trouble their charisma was causing me, indeed!
“Really, this puts Big Sister in a bind too, you know? Dealing with a self-proclaimed hero who talks this openly and then turns around and threatens me.”
“Since I have further activities planned, I’d like you to keep it quiet that I’m a hero, indeed.”
“How many demands are you going to pile on, you— …let’s see, the Spear Hero, was it?”
“I won’t be giving you my name, indeed.”
In my memory, Older Sister wore the same troubled expression even then.

“Well then… I’ll give you some advice, though I can’t promise it’ll work out well for Big Sister either. But if all you need is to delay them for a bit, there might be a way to manage that, don’t you think?”
“Do you have some method, then?”

Would Older Sister share with me some brilliant idea, the kind Father himself might have thought up in a flash? Somewhere in my head, someone was telling me not to just hand my thinking over to others, but there was no helping it—I was never very good at this sort of scheming. Of course, back when I had no means to fight, I used to rack my brain over strategy plenty, but once I became capable of handling things through strength, I’d stopped bothering, and now there was quite the blank in my skills!
“Listen. You don’t want the village fishermen going out to fish, right?”
“That’s right, indeed.”

“Honestly, it’d be better if Big Sister lured you into a trap herself… but I know perfectly well that’d be difficult given the simple matter of raw combat strength, which is why I’m answering you like this instead. I’d like you to understand that much, at least…”
“If you set a trap, I’ll simply have to make sure nobody in this territory can move at all, indeed.”
“I know that, which is exactly why I’m telling you to stop. Now, here’s the plan…”

And so it was that, having threatened Older Sister into working out a scheme for me, I set off on my next operation. It was the sort of trick the old me—before I ever became a hero—might have come up with. Aren’t you turning into even more of a meathead lately? I could almost hear Father saying, somewhere in my memory.
“Oh? Sadeena, finally back, are you?”
Older Sister returned to the village from her secret base, and Big Sister’s parents called out to her.
“Yes, I’m back. And speaking of which… there was a letter like this at my base.”
With that, Older Sister handed over to her parents the letter she’d had me write.
“A letter?”
Big Sister’s parent snatched up the letter at once, unfolded it, and their face went rigid. The contents of the letter read as follows.

Greetings to the people of Seaetto Territory. I am the one responsible for sinking the ship. It seems you intend to go out fishing, but should you do so, I cannot guarantee what might befall the people left behind in a territory with its manpower so diminished. My demand is but one: that you refrain from going out to fish. I can only hope this demand is met. No matter how tightly you fortify your defenses, it will be in vain. Give up.
And so, following Older Sister’s suggestion, I wrote the threatening letter and handed it over to her.
